assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles in laboratory culture respond to corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) by producing ACTH and alpha-MSH and secreting cortisol, regulated by an HPA-axis-like feedback loop.
assertions.quote: Thus, even in the absence of endocrine, neural, or vascular systemic connections, normal human scalp hair follicles directly respond to CRH stimulation in a strikingly similar manner to what is seen in the classical HPA axis, including synthesis and secretion of cortisol and activation of prototypic neuroendocrine feedback loops.
assertions.note: Cultured human hair follicles respond to CRH by producing ACTH and alpha-MSH, secreting cortisol, and exhibiting negative feedback.

assertions.text: Hair follicles operate an intrinsic growth hormone and IGF-1 loop.
assertions.note: The cited source for the somatotropic loop is unavailable, and the other available abstracts do not mention growth hormone or IGF-1.

assertions.text: Pattern hair loss is mediated by dihydrotestosterone (converted from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase) shrinking susceptible scalp follicles.
assertions.quote: Androgenetic alopecia, or male pattern hair loss, is a hair loss disorder mediated by dihydrotestosterone, the potent form of testosterone.
assertions.note: The source confirms androgenetic alopecia is mediated by dihydrotestosterone, but does not detail 5-alpha-reductase conversion or follicular miniaturization.

assertions.text: Growing hair follicles possess immune privilege protecting them from immune attack, and collapse of this immune privilege leads to alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: Collapse of anagen hair bulb IP is an essential prerequisite for the development of alopecia areata (AA).
assertions.note: Anagen hair follicles have immune privilege, and its collapse is an essential prerequisite for alopecia areata development.

units.text:
Human evidence
Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
When immune privilege fails, the attack runs through cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors block. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.
adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)
At 36 weeks, 36–39% on the higher dose had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo
What it means: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any peptide. Both t…

What changes in practice
Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.
Pattern, trigger, patches and androgens decide the treatment. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the US, as of September 2026, topical minoxidil is FDA-approved and sold over the counter, finasteride for pattern hair loss is a prescription drug, and baricitinib is approved for adults with severe alopecia areata.

units.text:
Lesson 5.2 · Concept
Five receptors, one family of hormones.
Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.
MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: brain, appetite and sexual response
Narration: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for AC…

assertions.text: Skin produces proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cleaves it into ACTH, α-MSH, and β-endorphin, with skin cells also carrying the corresponding receptors.
assertions.quote: In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin. Demonstration of the corresponding receptors in the same cells suggests para- or autocrine mechanisms of action.
assertions.note: Slominski and Wortsman describe local cutaneous production of POMC, ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin along with corresponding cellular receptors.

assertions.text: Melanocortin peptides act on five melanocortin receptors.
assertions.quote: The 5 known melanocortin receptors (MCs) have established physiological roles.
assertions.note: Laiho and Murray confirm the 5 known melanocortin receptors.

assertions.text: MC1R regulates pigmentation in skin and hair.
assertions.quote: MC 1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC 2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC 3 and MC 4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC 5 regulates sebogenesis.

MC3R has been linked to timing of sexual maturation and linear growth. Some studies have reported the association between MC4R and sexual function.

units.text:
Four registers
One receptor family, two very different molecules.
Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
Mechanism
Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective
Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain
Human evidence
Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D
Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.
Regulatory status
Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019 · Melanotan II: none
Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication anywhere.
Ope…

units.text:
The evidence
Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes severe pain within minutes. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.
69 vs 41 h
median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)
Langendonk et al., NEJM 2015 · European trial, 74 adults: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months
What it means: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, o…

Patients have severe burning pain, typically on the hands and face, and this pain is often followed by swelling and redness.

units.text:
Safety signals
What the case reports show.
The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.
Skin: changing moles, eruptive naevi, melanonychia
Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy
Narration: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and revie…

Fictional case
New moles after a summer of tanning shots.
A 27-year-old attends for a skin-quality consultation and mentions injecting a 'tanning peptide' bought online for three months. She has noticed darker moles, several new small ones and a dark stripe along one fingernail. Her mother had melanoma. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.
Almost certainly Melanotan II: approved nowhere, unknown strength and purity
New and changing naevi and nail pigmentation are the documented harms
Family history of melanoma: the guide's absolute contraindication

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Reassure her: darker moles are expected with a tan. Review them at her next routine visit.
Explanation: New and changing naevi are the documented harm here, dermoscopic changes on Melanotan II can mimic melanoma, and her family history raises the stakes.
Correct answer: Advise stopping now, record the product and seller, examine the whole skin and nails with dermoscopy and baseline photographs if your setting allows, and refer promptly to dermatology.
Explanation: Right. Stop the exposure, document it, and have the changing naevi and the nail band assessed and followed. Even the approved MC1R agonist comes with twice-yearly skin examinations, and she has a family history of melanoma.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Offer afamelanotide instead, as the approved version of the same drug.
Explanation: Afamelano…

units.text:
Regulatory status
Three regulators, one answer.
Each statement below is dated, because regulatory status changes. None of the three regulators has approved Melanotan II, and each has put its concerns on the record. UK and EU mapping for the rest of this course is still in progress.
United States · FDA (page current as of 22 April 2026)
Unapproved; nomination withdrawn
FDA's compounding safety page lists Melanotan II among substances withdrawn from Category 2, citing impurity and immunogenicity risks and published reports of melanoma, encephalopathy, sympathomimetic toxicity and priapism
United Kingdom · MHRA (17 April 2024)
Unauthorised medicine
Injectable products are classed as medicines; MHRA advises anyone using them to stop immediately and has removed melanotan products from sale for over ten years
Australia · TGA (17 August 2026)
Prescription-only; no approved product
Not approved …

units.text:
A patient says, 'Afamelanotide is approved, so Melanotan II is basically the same drug.' What is the accurate reply?
Explanation: Name the molecule, then its indication: approval does not transfer between them.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes. They act on the same receptor, so the approval covers both.
Explanation: Sharing MC1R does not make them the same molecule, and an approval attaches to one product and one indication.
Correct answer: They are different molecules. Afamelanotide is approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II acts on several receptors, is approved nowhere, and is linked in case reports to changing moles and priapism.
Explanation: Correct. Same family, different selectivity, different evidence and different legal standing.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II is safe if it comes from a reputable seller.
Explanat…

units.text:
Lesson 5.3 · Concept
A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment of the HIV Tat protein to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.
PTD-DBM: releases a Wnt brake (mouse data)
Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide
Both: mechanism first, human data absent
Narration: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy…
units.sourceNote: Lee 2017 (J Invest Dermatol) · Dardenne 1982 · Peptide Pocket Guide

assertions.text: PTD-DBM incorporates a cell-penetrating fragment derived from the HIV Tat protein.

By disrupting this binding, the CXXC5-Dvl complex no longer forms and can, therefore, not disrupt the downstream signaling of Wnt/β-catenin, ultimately enhancing the effects of this signaling pathway.
assertions.note: Mehta 2025 states that PTD-DBM disrupts CXXC5 binding to Dishevelled and activates downstream Wnt/β-catenin signalling.

units.text:
The evidence
Zero trials in people.

Module 06 · The growth-hormone axis and the skin
Real endocrinology, borrowed for marketing.
Growth hormone and IGF-1 genuinely shape skin, and one peptide on this axis has approval-grade trials. Most of what patients are offered has much less behind it. In three lessons you will separate the physiology from the promise, the approved from the anecdotal, and the side-effects you can see from the risks nobody has measured.

Growth hormone and IGF-1 in skin homeostasis
GHRH analogues and s…

Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
Two hormones, two layers of skin.
Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age

Human evidence
The skin result that started it all.
In 1990 a New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.

What changes in practice
Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence.

units.text:
Lesson 6.2 · Concept
One axis, four ways in.
Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.
Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues
Narration: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor ag…
units.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 · Peptide Pocket Guide, growth-hormone axis · Dominikowski 2026

assertions.text: Somatropin is growth hormone itself, produced using recombinant technology.
assertions.quote: Somatropin is a human growth hormone produced by recombinant DNA technology in Escherichia coli.
assertions.note: Genotropin prescribing information defines somatropin as human growth hormone produced by recombinant DNA technology.

assertions.text: GHRH analogues, including sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295, stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor to induce pulsatile endogenous growth hormone secretion.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing hormone (GHRH) analogues are synthetic peptides designed to stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the pituitary GHRH receptor, thereby increasing GH pulsatility and secondarily IGF-1.
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 confirms that GHRH analogues activate the pituitary GHRH receptor to stimulate endogenous pulsatile GH secretion.

assertions.text: Ghrelin-receptor agonists (including ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, and oral ibutamoren/MK-677) stimulate GH release through the ghrelin receptor on the hypothalamus and pituitary.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing peptides (GHRPs) are short synthetic peptides that stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the ghrelin receptor - the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR-1a), at the level of the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary.
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 states that growth hormone secretagogues activate the ghrelin receptor (GHSR-1a) at the hypothalamic and pituitary level.

assertions.text: IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary and act directly on the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: The final group discussed in this review comprises IGF-1 analogues, represented here by pegylated mechano growth factor (PEG-MGF) and IGF-1 LR3 (insulin-like growth factor-1, long [Arg3]). These compounds act primarily through the IGF-1R, a transmembrane receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity that mediates many of the downstream “somatomedin” effects of IGF-1, as outlined earlier in this manuscript.
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 confirms that IGF-1 analogues like IGF-1 LR3 act directly via the IGF-1 receptor rather than through pituitary GH secretion.

The evidence
Zero skin trials.
A PubMed search in September 2026 found no randomized trial with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3. The closest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue closely related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults: skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.

Closest: a 1997 single-blind study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue, 19 older adults, skin thickness by caliper
What it means: Every skin promise made for these peptides rests on mechanism and anecdote. The nearest data are one small study without a parallel control group (D).
What it does not mean: It does not show these peptides harm skin or do nothing for it. It shows the question has never been…

units.text:
Lesson 6.3 · Recognition
What too much growth hormone looks like.
Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs: fluid retention with swelling, joint pain, tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present.
Soft tissue: puffy, thickened face, hands and feet

units.text:
Four registers
Does raising IGF-1 cause cancer?
The honest answer has four parts, and each has its own source. Keep them apart, or a mechanism will be heard as a measured risk.
Mechanism
Plausible
IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, which gives any IGF-1-raising product a theoretical concern
Human observation
Modest associations
In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 goes with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal and thyroid cancer; reverse causation is not excluded. People with GH-receptor deficiency have very little cancer.
Acromegaly
Slightly raised, inconsistently
Pooled studies show about 1.5 times the expected cancer incidence, inflated by small single-centre series; a Danish nationwide cohort found no clear rise
GH replacement
Largely reassuring
No clear raised risk in 23,984 GH-treated children with growth failure and no other diseas…
units.sourceNote: Renehan 2004 · Knuppel 2020 · Dal 2018 · Swerdlow 2017 · Boguszewski 2022 · Guevara-Aguirre 2011

assertions.text: IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, giving IGF-1-raising products theoretical oncologic concern.
assertions.quote: IGF−1 receptor signaling activates proliferative and anti−apoptotic pathways, including PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK, and contributes to cell−cycle progression, survival, and invasion ( 160 – 163 ).
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 confirms that IGF-1 receptor signalling activates proliferative and anti-apoptotic pathways, underpinning theoretical oncologic concerns.

assertions.text: In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 is associated with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal and thyroid cancer.
assertions.quote: Higher IGF-I concentration was associated with increased risks of thyroid cancer [HR per 5 nmol/L higher concentration 1.18; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.37] in addition to colorectal (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.03-1.13), breast (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.07-1.15), and prostate cancer (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.05-1.12), and reduced risks of ovarian and liver cancer.
assertions.note: Knuppel 2020 found higher IGF-I was associated with increased risks of thyroid, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer.

assertions.text: In large studies linking natural IGF-1 to cancer risks, reverse causation is not excluded.
assertions.quote: Mean follow-up was 6.9 years and the possibility that the observed associations may be influenced by reverse causality bias cannot be excluded.
assertions.note: Knuppel 2020 explicitly notes that the possibility of reverse causality bias cannot be excluded.

assertions.quote: The individuals with GHR deficiency (GHRD) exhibited only one non-lethal malignancy and no cases of diabetes, in contrast to 17% cancer and 5% diabetes prevalence in the controls.
assertions.note: Guevara-Aguirre 2011 observed only one non-lethal malignancy in GHRD subjects over 22 years of monitoring.

assertions.text: A Danish nationwide cohort of patients with acromegaly found no clear rise in cancer incidence.
assertions.quote: The cohort study identified 81 cases of cancer after exclusion of cases diagnosed within the first year [SIR 1.1; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.9 to 1.4].
assertions.note: Dal 2018 reports a nationwide cohort standardized incidence ratio of 1.1 (95% CI 0.9 to 1.4).

Evidence, regulation and compliance · three lessons
Lesson 7.1 Grading the evidence behind an aesthetic claim · Lesson 7.2 Compounding law, the 40-amino-acid line and certificates of analysis · Lesson 7.3 Cosmetic, compounded or investigational: consent and the chart.
Module 07 · Evidence, regulation and compliance
Grade it, check it, write it down.
This last module turns the course into three habits. You will rate the certainty behind a claim with GRADE, read a compounding status and a certificate of analysis for what they do and do not prove, and write the consent and chart note that an unapproved product needs. The regulatory detail is US; UK and EU mapping for this course is still in progress.

Lesson 7.1 · Concept
GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.
GRADE sorts the evidence on a specific question into four levels of certainty: high, moderate, low and very low. The rating applies to a body of evidence for one outcome, never to a single study or to a molecule. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low; certainty then falls for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias, and occasionally rises for a very large effect. Both Hormonaly guides print the letters A to D for the same idea, adapted, and attach each letter to a specific use.
Four levels, applied to a body of evidence
Five named reasons to rate down
The letter belongs to a use, never to a molecule
Narration: Every claim you hear about a skin peptide carries a hidden question. How sure can we be? GRADE answers it with four levels of cert…

units.text:
Who paid
Sponsored studies come out better.
A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways. Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks. It is the pattern you met with oral collagen in module 04.
1.27
risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result, industry-sponsored versus other studies
Lundh et al., Cochrane 2017 · 95% CI 1.17–1.37 · moderate-certainty evidence
What it means: When a manufacturer pays for the trial, a favourable result is more likely. Funding is a reason to read a trial harder and to look for independent replication.
What it does not mean: It does not make a sponsored trial wrong or an independent one right. It describes an average ti…

assertions.text: A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways.

assertions.text: Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks.
assertions.quote: Sponsorship of drug and device studies by the manufacturing company leads to more favorable efficacy results and conclusions than sponsorship by other sources. Our analyses suggest the existence of an industry bias that cannot be explained by standard 'Risk of bias' assessments.
assertions.note: The authors conclude that industry sponsorship yields more favourable efficacy results and conclusions, which is not explained by standard risk-of-bias tools.

units.text:
Worked example
Name what lowers certainty.
GRADE names the ways a body of evidence can mislead. Read the four you will use most. Then sort four cases from this course by the reason that most lowers certainty. The fifth, publication bias, is suspected when the evidence is a handful of small, mostly commercially funded studies.
Risk of bias
How the trials were run
Flaws in design or conduct that can exaggerate an effect; check whether low- and high-quality trials disagree
Inconsistency
The trials disagree
Unexplained differences in results between studies of the same question
Indirectness
A different question answered
The studies differ from your question in population, intervention, comparison or outcome
Imprecision
Too little data
Too few people or events; the confidence interval spans an important effect and little or none
Callout: Name the reason and you can explain a grade to a patien…

assertions.text: In GRADE, publication bias is suspected when the evidence is a handful of small, mostly commercially funded studies.
assertions.quote: For publication bias, a body of evidence comprising small studies funded by industry should raise suspicion.
assertions.note: Core GRADE 4 states that a body of evidence consisting of small industry-funded studies raises suspicion of publication bias.

assertions.text: Risk of bias in GRADE relates to flaws in trial design or conduct that can exaggerate an effect, assessed in part by checking whether low- and high-quality trials disagree.
assertions.quote: Decisions regarding rating down for risk of bias will depend on the weights of high and low risk of bias studies and similarities or differences between the results of high and low risk of bias studies.
assertions.note: Core GRADE 4 notes rating down depends on differences between low and high risk of bias studies.

assertions.text: Inconsistency in GRADE refers to unexplained differences in results between studies addressing the same question.
assertions.quote: This third article in a seven part series presents the Core GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach to deciding whether to rate down certainty of evidence due to inconsistency—that is, unexplained variability in results across studies.
assertions.note: Core GRADE 3 defines inconsistency as unexplained variability in results across studies.

assertions.text: Indirectness occurs when the available studies differ from the clinical question in population, intervention, comparison, or outcome (PICO).
assertions.quote: When target and study PICOs differ substantially, studies provide indirect evidence and Core GRADE users may rate down the certainty of evidence as a result of this indirectness.
assertions.note: Core GRADE 5 confirms rating down for indirectness occurs when study and target PICOs differ substantially.

assertions.text: Imprecision in GRADE involves too little data where the confidence interval spans both an important effect and little or no effect.
assertions.quote: For instance, using the MID thresholds, a point estimate greater than the MID suggests an important effect and less than the MID, an unimportant or little to no effect. Users then rate down for imprecision if the 95% confidence interval crosses the MID for benefit or harm.
assertions.note: Core GRADE 2 explains rating down for imprecision when confidence intervals cross the threshold between important and unimportant/little to no effect.

What changes in practice
Two checks, never one.
Evidence grade and regulatory status are separate axes, and both Hormonaly guides ask you to clear both. An approved drug can carry a low grade for the use a patient wants, and a compound with stronger human data can still have no lawful route. A plausible mechanism never raises a grade. Say the outcome, the grade and who ran the trials, then check the status as its own step.
Grade: certainty for this outcome
Status: what the law allows, checked separately
Mechanism never raises a grade
Narration: When a patient asks whether a peptide works, start with the outcome they care about, say fewer lines around the eyes, and give the certainty for that outcome, along with who paid for the trials behind it. Then, as a separate step, check what the product legally is. The Hormonaly guides keep these two checks apart for a reason. An approved drug can…

A fictional serum's brochure says 'GRADE A: three randomized trials'. All three were run by the maker, enrolled 20 to 30 people each, lasted four weeks and measured skin hydration. Your patient wants fewer wrinkles. What is the most defensible certainty for that outcome?
Explanation: Grade the outcome the patient wants, then name what lowers it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): High, because three randomized trials agree.
Explanation: Randomized trials start high, but these are small, sponsor-run and measured a different outcome, and each of those lowers certainty.
Correct answer: Low or very low: small sponsor-run trials that measured hydration, not wrinkles.
Explanation: Correct. Indirectness (the wrong outcome), imprecision (few people) and suspected publication bias (small industry-funded studies) all rate it down.

assertions.note: Supported by Core GRADE 5.

assertions.quote: For publication bias, a body of evidence comprising small studies funded by industry should raise suspicion.
assertions.note: Supported by Core GRADE 4.

units.text:
Lesson 7.2 · Concept
Two compounding routes, one strict order.
In the US, section 503A lets a licensed pharmacist or physician compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use and good manufacturing practice. The bulk substance must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list. It must also come from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice under inspection, and may compound without patient-specific prescriptions.
503A: patient-specific, three exemptions
Monograph, then approved component, then the bulks list
503B: registered, inspected, held to good manufacturing practice
Narration: The United States has two routes for compoundi…

Peptide or biologic
Forty amino acids.
Since 23 March 2020 FDA defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of more than 40 amino acids, whether or not it is chemically synthesized, so anything above the line is a biological product. On that date tesamorelin, a 44-residue GHRH analogue, and the enzyme hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences, and FDA told compounders that transitioned biologics cannot use the 503A or 503B exemptions.
amino acids: above this, FDA treats the molecule as a protein, and so as a biological product
85 FR 10057, effective 23 March 2020 · tesamorelin (44 residues) and hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences
What it means: Size decides the rulebook. Peptides of 40 or fewer alpha amino acids stay drugs, so the 503A questions apply; above 40 the product is a biologic, and the compounding exemptions are closed to it.

units.text:
Concept
What a certificate can and cannot prove.
A certificate of analysis is the supplier's own report on a named lot. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate prints the expected mass beside the observed one. HPLC gives purity as a percentage, which says nothing about what the impurities are. Endotoxin, microbial, water, counter-ion, metal and solvent results complete it. A certificate cannot prove that the vial in your hand came from that lot, how it was stored since, or that it is sterile and suitable to inject.
Identity: mass spectrometry, observed against expected
Purity: an HPLC percentage, impurities unnamed
Suitability to inject needs sterility, endotoxin and the right lot

The appropriate way to establish the endotoxins limit is to use the calculation methods provided in the USP or AAMI standards.

What changes in practice
Research use only is a label, and never a route.
In the US, 'not for use in humans' labelling lets a supplier ship an investigational drug for laboratory or in-vitro research, and obliges the shipper to check that is how it will be used. FDA reads intended use from claims, marketing and the circumstances of sale, so the disclaimer changes nothing about a vial sold with injection instructions. A certificate cannot turn such a product into a pharmaceutical.
The label permits laboratory research only
Intended use is read from how a product is sold
A certificate cannot convert a research product

units.text:
Lesson 7.3 · Concept
Off-label needs a label.
Off-label prescribing means using an approved drug for a use its labelling does not cover, and FDA accepts it as clinical judgment. A never-approved peptide has no label to depart from, so prescribing it is use of an unapproved drug. Introducing an unapproved new drug into interstate commerce is a prohibited act under the FD&C Act, and FDA's 2020 warning letter to a compounding pharmacy named BPC-157 and GHK-Cu on exactly this basis.
Off-label applies only to approved drugs
Compounded is still unapproved
Narration: Off-label is the phrase to get right first. FDA uses it for an approved drug prescribed outside its labelling, which prescribers generally may do when they judge it medically appropriate. Some examples are claims that products will restore hair growth, reduce cellulite, treat varicose veins, increase or decrease the production of melanin (pigment) in the skin, or regenerate cells.

assertions.text: The term 'cosmeceutical' has no legal meaning under the FD&C Act.
assertions.quote: The FD&C Act does not recognize any such category as "cosmeceuticals." A product can be a drug, a cosmetic, or a combination of both, but the term "cosmeceutical" has no meaning under the law.
assertions.note: FDA explicitly notes that the FD&C Act does not recognize the term cosmeceutical.

assertions.text: For dietary supplements, the manufacturer is responsible for evaluating safety and labelling before marketing, and the FDA takes regulatory action after products reach the market.
assertions.quote: That means that these firms are responsible for evaluating the safety and labeling of their products before marketing to ensure that they meet all the requirements of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act as amended by DSHEA and FDA regulations.
assertions.note: FDA dietary supplement overview confirms manufacturers evaluate safety/labeling before sale and FDA acts post-market.

assertions.text: Prescribing an approved drug for an unapproved (off-label) indication is lawful clinical judgment from the FDA perspective.
assertions.quote: From the FDA perspective, once the FDA approves a drug, healthcare providers generally may prescribe the drug for an unapproved use when they judge that it is medically appropriate for their patient.
assertions.note: FDA confirms healthcare providers may generally prescribe approved drugs off-label when deemed medically appropriate.

assertions.text: Non-injectable GHK-Cu is placed in 503A Category 1.
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: The FDA 503A categories document lists GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes) under Category 1.

'Just prescribe it off-label.'
A 52-year-old patient, three weeks after a fractional laser treatment, asks you to prescribe compounded BPC-157 injections 'off-label' to speed healing. She has found a pharmacy willing to make it and shows you its certificate of analysis. This is a fictional case built from the module's sources, and one response is clearly best.
BPC-157 has no approval, so there is no label to go off
It has no 503A route; FDA staff advised against listing it
A certificate describes a lot and creates no route

Correct answer: Decline to prescribe it. Explain the evidence and the US status in plain terms, return to the aftercare plan her treating clinician set, and record her request, what you explained and her decision.
Explanation: Right. You keep the conversation, give her the real category and the grade, and leave a chart note a reviewer can follow.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Suggest she buy research-grade BPC-157 with a good certificate and come back for monitoring.

Documentation
A chart note a reviewer can follow.

What it is
Article and status, in those words
For example 'not FDA-approved; no 503A route', never 'off-label'
If compounded
Pathway, facility, certificate
503A or 503B, the pharmacy, and the certificate of analysis relied on
Consent
Four elements, in writing
Not approved for this use; foreseeable risks; approved alternatives, including doing nothing; what happens if harm occurs
Evidence
Outcome and grade
The certainty you quoted, for the outcome you discussed
Plan
Monitoring and a stopping rule
What you will watch, and when you will stop
Status check
Dated
The day you checked the FDA lists; they changed in April and May…

units.text:
GHK-Cu appears in three products: a cream sold 'for the look of fine lines', the same cream sold 'to regenerate skin cells', and an injectable vial labelled research use only. In the US, which statement is right?
Explanation: Name the claim and the route, then the regime.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are cosmetics, because the molecule is the same.
Explanation: The regime follows the claim and the route. A structure-or-function claim makes the second cream a drug, and the vial is no cosmetic at all.
Correct answer: The first is a cosmetic; the second makes a drug claim, so it is an unapproved drug; the vial is outside any clinical route.
Explanation: Correct. Claim and route decide the rulebook, whatever the molecule.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are lawful, because GHK-Cu is in Category 1.
Explanation: Category 1 covers 503A compound…

assertions.text: Under FDA regulation, a structure-or-function claim such as regenerating cells establishes a topical product's intended use as a drug rather than a cosmetic.
assertions.quote: Such claims establish the product as a drug because the intended use is to treat or prevent disease or otherwise affect the structure or functions of the human body. Some examples are claims that products will restore hair growth, reduce cellulite, treat varicose veins, increase or decrease the production of melanin (pigment) in the skin, or regenerate cells.

units.text:
Closing Module 7: which statement keeps evidence, regulatory status and product quality apart?
Explanation: Grade, status and quality: three checks, never one sentence.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The certificate shows 99% purity, so the peptide is evidence-based and fine to compound.
Explanation: That blends product quality into evidence and legality. Purity says nothing about whether it works or whether any route is lawful.
Correct answer: Topical GHK-Cu: small-trial evidence (C); in the US, non-injectable use sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation; its certificate can show identity and purity, never sterility or legality.
Explanation: Correct. Three separate answers, each with its own source.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): GHK-Cu is in Category 1, so it is approved for skin and the evidence question is settled.
Explanation: Category 1 is an enforcem…

assertions.text: In the US, non-injectable GHK-Cu is listed in 503A Category 1 as a bulk drug substance under evaluation.
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: FDA Category 1 includes GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes of administration under evaluation.

assertions.text: Evidence for topical GHK-Cu is derived from small clinical trials.
assertions.quote: Thirteen patients completed the study.
assertions.note: The cited clinical trial of topical GHK-Cu evaluated 13 patients.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis can document identity and purity but does not establish product sterility or legal authorization.
assertions.note: The provided source texts do not address what a certificate of analysis can or cannot verify regarding sterility or legality.

recheck.note: The provided source texts discuss certificates of analysis in specific compounding evaluations but do not state that a certificate of analysis does not establish product sterility or legal authorization.

units.text:
A single-cell RNA atlas predicts that a skin cell type can make a hormone. What would move that finding toward proof of secretion?
Explanation: Transcriptomic maps predict capacity; secretion and function need protein-level and functional evidence, and clinical use needs human trials.
Correct answer: Showing the hormone protein and its release by those cells, then its effect in tissue or in people.
Explanation: Correct. RNA is the first rung; protein, release and function are the next.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the same RNA in a second atlas.
Explanation: Replicating the RNA confirms the transcript, which is still a prediction about secretion.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the hormone's receptor RNA in neighbouring cells.
Explanation: That predicts a possible receiver; it does not show the hormone is made or released.

assertions.text: Transcriptomic maps and predictions based on RNA data are putative and require protein-level, in vitro, or in vivo functional validation to demonstrate hormone secretion and action.
assertions.quote: Important: these predictions are based on transcriptomic data and should be considered as putative and hypothesis-generating, rather than as functional hormones and receptors. The user takes responsibility for validation using appropriate methods (e.g. in vitro, in vivo) and for describing appropriately their use of transcriptome-based scores and predictions.
assertions.note: The Hormone Cell Atlas portal explicitly notes that transcriptomic predictions should be treated as putative and require validation via appropriate in vitro and in vivo functional methods.

units.text:
Which finding is a local cutaneous feedback loop rather than systemic endocrine signalling?
Explanation: A local loop is made and used within the skin; systemic signals travel through the blood, in either direction.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Skin-made vitamin D3 carried by the blood to the liver and kidney.
Explanation: That is the skin supplying a whole-body hormone system: skin to body.
Correct answer: Human scalp follicles in culture secrete cortisol and then reduce their own CRH.
Explanation: Correct. Made, sensed and fed back within the follicle, with no systemic connection.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Thin skin and striae in Cushing syndrome.
Explanation: Circulating cortisol excess acting on the skin: body to skin.

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles in culture secrete cortisol and down-regulate their own CRH expression via local feedback.
assertions.quote: Finally, human hair follicles display HPA axis-like regulatory feedback systems, since the glucocorticoid receptor agonist hydrocortisone down-regulates follicular CRH expression.
assertions.note: Cultured human hair follicles secrete cortisol and down-regulate CRH expression via glucocorticoid feedback.

units.text:
Why can a blood or saliva cortisol level not tell you how much cortisol a patient's skin is generating?
Explanation: Local tissue cortisol and systemic cortisol are separate: the first is a research mechanism, the second is what diagnostic tests measure.
Correct answer: Because 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
Explanation: Correct: a mechanism shown in human skin samples and mice.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because skin cells cannot make or activate cortisol.
Explanation: They can: skin expresses an HPA-like axis, and 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol locally.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because saliva and blood cortisol tests are unreliable for everything.
Explanation: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line test for Cushing's syndrome; it measures systemic cort…

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local glucocorticoid availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
assertions.quote: Within target tissues, GC availability is regulated at a prereceptor level, independently of systemic levels, by isozymes of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (11β-HSD) that interconvert active cortisol and inactive cortisone.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms 11β-HSD1 activates cortisol in human skin cells and regulates glucocorticoid availability independently of systemic levels.

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 activity and expression were demonstrated in human skin samples and mice.
assertions.quote: 11β-HSD1 (which activates cortisol), but not 11β-HSD2 (which inactivates cortisol), was expressed in epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts in human skin and also in outer hair follicle root sheath cells in murine skin. 11β-HSD1 activity was present ex vivo in both species and increased with age in human skin tissue explants.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms 11β-HSD1 expression and activity in epidermal/dermal cells in human skin and murine hair follicle sheath cells.

assertions.text: Skin expresses an HPA-like axis.
assertions.note: The cited abstracts do not mention a skin HPA-like axis.

assertions.text: Late-night salivary cortisol is a recommended first-line diagnostic test for Cushing's syndrome.
assertions.quote: We recommend initial use of one test with high diagnostic accuracy (urine cortisol, late night salivary cortisol, 1 mg overnight or 2 mg 48-h dexamethasone suppression test).
assertions.note: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends late-night salivary cortisol as one initial test with high diagnostic accuracy for Cushing's syndrome.

units.text:
A patient asks whether starting hormone therapy at menopause will stop her wrinkles. Which answer fits the evidence?
Explanation: Separate structural effects (small trials) from visible ageing (large trials) and from indications (symptoms and bone).
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes: estrogen rebuilds collagen, so her wrinkles will improve.
Explanation: Small trials show thicker skin, but the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles.
Correct answer: It may thicken the skin a little, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not a reason to start; hot flashes or vaginal symptoms are worth discussing with a prescriber.
Explanation: Correct: a secondary effect, and an indication-led decision.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): It has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: Small RCTs do show gains in thickness and collagen; what is unpro…

assertions.text: Trials show hormone therapy can increase skin thickness.
assertions.quote: The results may help postmenopausal women to better appraise the benefits of estrogen replacement therapy, and they provide further evidence of the potential of conjugated estrogens in preventing skin aging.
assertions.note: A randomized, double-blind study demonstrated significant increases in skin thickness with conjugated estrogens.

assertions.text: Large trials evaluating hormone therapy found no statistically significant difference or improvement in facial wrinkles compared to placebo.
assertions.quote: Low-dose hormone therapy for 48 weeks in postmenopausal women did not significantly alter mild to moderate age-related facial skin changes.
assertions.note: A 485-subject RCT found no significant difference in facial wrinkling between hormone therapy and placebo.

assertions.text: Hot flashes (vasomotor symptoms) and vaginal symptoms are established indications to consider discussing hormone therapy.
assertions.quote: Hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms (VMS) and the genitourinary syndrome of menopause and has been shown to prevent bone loss and fracture.
assertions.note: The NAMS position statement confirms hormone therapy as the most effective treatment for vasomotor and genitourinary symptoms.

units.text:
Which statement about topical GHK-Cu keeps its evidence and its regulatory status apart correctly?
Explanation: Mechanism, human evidence and regulatory status are separate registers; GHK-Cu scores differently on each.
Correct answer: It is GRADE C on small trials, and in the US its non-injectable form sits in 503A Category 1, which means under evaluation.
Explanation: Correct. Two separate answers: small-trial human evidence, and an enforcement posture that is not an approval.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its Category 1 listing shows FDA has found it effective for skin.
Explanation: Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating; it says nothing about efficacy.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its copper-enzyme mechanism makes its evidence grade A.
Explanation: A plausible mechanism is not human evidence; the trials are small (C).

assertions.text: In the United States, the non-injectable form of GHK-Cu is placed in 503A Category 1, which designates bulk drug substances under evaluation.
assertions.quote:
FDA has added the following bulk drug substance to category 1 for the reason provided below: 
 
 o “GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) ” - GHK-Cu (except for injectable 
routes of administration) was removed from c ategory 1 on April 22, 2026, because the 
nominations for GHK-Cu were withdrawn by the nominators.
assertions.note: FDA 503A list classifies non-injectable GHK-Cu under Category 1: Bulk Drug Substances Under Evaluation.

assertions.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is rated GRADE C based on small trials.
assertions.note: The cited reference guide is unavailable and the included trial abstract does not mention a formal GRADE C rating.

units.text:
Oral collagen trials pooled together look positive. What did splitting them by funding and quality show?
Explanation: Funding and study quality can explain a pooled effect; ask who ran the trial before what it showed.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The benefit held in every subgroup.
Explanation: It did not: independent and high-quality trials showed no effect.
Correct answer: The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and lower-quality trials.
Explanation: Correct — Myung and Park, 2025, 23 RCTs.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Independent trials showed harm.
Explanation: No harm signal was reported; the finding is about absence of benefit.

assertions.text: In a meta-analysis of 23 RCTs by Myung et al. (2025), splitting trials by funding and quality showed that independent and high-quality trials found no significant benefit, whereas pharmaceutical-funded and lower-quality trials showed significant effects.
assertions.quote: However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects. Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: Subgroup analyses in Myung (2025) found that independent and high-quality trials showed no effect, whereas pharma-funded and low-quality trials showed significant improvements.

units.text:
Which statement about afamelanotide and Melanotan II is accurate?
Explanation: Approval attaches to a specific product and indication; a shared receptor transfers neither evidence nor legal standing.
Correct answer: Afamelanotide is approved (EU 2014, US 2019) only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II is approved for no indication, and regulators in the US, UK and Australia have warned about it.
Explanation: Correct. Same receptor family, different molecules, and only one has an approval, for one rare disease.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Afamelanotide's US approval covers cosmetic tanning.
Explanation: The US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; tanning is not an approved use.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II became approvable once FDA reviewed it for compounding.
Explanation: Its compounding nominat…

assertions.text: Afamelanotide was approved in the EU in 2014 for erythropoietic protoporphyria.
assertions.quote: The European Commission granted a marketing authorisation valid throughout the European Union for Scenesse on 22 December 2014.
assertions.note: The EMA EPAR confirms that marketing authorization for Scenesse (afamelanotide) for EPP was issued in December 2014.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide received US approval in 2019 for erythropoietic protoporphyria.
assertions.note: The cited FDA label source is unavailable, and the remaining provided sources do not document US approval.

assertions.text: Melanotan II has no approved indications and regulators in the US, UK, and Australia have issued safety warnings about it.
assertions.quote: These products may cause serious side effects, so our advice to those who have used Melanotan II injections or nasal sprays is to stop using them immediately and if you have suffered side effects, speak to your doctor and report them to the MHRA through our Yellow Card Scheme.
assertions.note: US and UK regulatory warnings and unapproved status are documented, but the Australian TGA advisory source is unavailable.

assertions.text: Melanotan II's compounding nomination was withdrawn, and the FDA lists serious safety risks associated with it.
assertions.quote: Compounded drugs containing Melanotan II may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration due to the potential for aggregation or peptide-related impurities. Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.

units.text:
A patient asks about a PTD-DBM hair spray. Which grade fits its evidence, and why?
Explanation: Grade the human evidence, then say who produced it; a strong mechanism with no trial in people is D.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A, because it acts on the central Wnt pathway of hair growth.
Explanation: A plausible pathway is mechanism, and grades rest on human evidence.
Correct answer: D: one 2017 study in mice and scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial published or registered as of September 2026.
Explanation: Correct. Animal and tissue data only, from one group with a commercial link.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): C, because small human trials show regrowth.
Explanation: No human trial of PTD-DBM exists, small or large.

assertions.text: A 2017 study demonstrated that targeting CXXC5 with a competitor peptide (PTD-DBM) accelerates hair regrowth in mice and investigated its mechanism in human scalp tissue and dermal papilla cells.
assertions.quote: Disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction with a competitor peptide activated the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and accelerated hair regrowth and wound-induced hair follicle neogenesis.
assertions.note: Lee et al. (2017) demonstrated that disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction with a competitor peptide activated Wnt/β-catenin signaling and accelerated hair regrowth in mice and examined CXXC5 in human balding scalps.

assertions.text: PTD-DBM evidence for hair regrowth remains limited to preclinical and mouse models, with no published human clinical trials.
assertions.quote: A study by Lee et al. has shown that applying PTD-DBM topically enhances hair regrowth in mouse models of androgenetic alopecia [ 21 ].
assertions.note: Mehta et al. note that topical PTD-DBM has only been demonstrated to enhance hair regrowth in mouse models, with work restricted to rodent models.

units.text:
In the US, as of September 2026, which statement about growth-hormone secretagogues and 503A compounding is accurate?
Explanation: Popularity and compounding volume are not regulatory standing; check the live FDA lists and name the date.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Ipamorelin and CJC-1295 are on the 503A bulks list, because clinics compound them widely.
Explanation: Neither is on the list. FDA's advisory committee voted against ipamorelin in 2024, and both 503A nominations were withdrawn.
Correct answer: None of them is on the 503A bulks list; ibutamoren is in FDA's Category 2 for a heart-failure signal, and the ipamorelin and CJC-1295 nominations were withdrawn.
Explanation: Correct, dated to FDA's category documents of April and May 2026.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Sermorelin is an FDA-approved product marketed for adult anti-ageing.
Explanation: No…

assertions.text: FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted against placing ipamorelin on the 503A Bulks List in 2024.
assertions.quote: The majority of the Committee members voted against placing Ipamorelin acetate on the 503A Bulks List for the same reasons as stated for Ipamorelin (free base).
assertions.note: The PCAC minutes from October 29, 2024, document that the committee voted against including ipamorelin acetate and ipamorelin free base on the 503A bulks list.

assertions.text: The 503A nominations for ipamorelin and CJC-1295 were withdrawn by their nominators.
assertions.quote: This list of bulk drug substances previously in category 2 of the interim policies were withdrawn by the nominators.
assertions.note: FDA's Category 2 safety risks webpage lists both CJC-1295 and ipamorelin acetate among substances previously in Category 2 that were withdrawn by nominators.

assertions.text: Ibutamoren is placed in FDA Category 2 due to a safety signal for congestive heart failure.
assertions.quote: Ibutamoren mesylate poses significant safety risks due to the potential for congestive heart failure in certain patients. The agency is aware of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial assessing ibutamoren mesylate for the treatment of patients recovering from hip fracture that “was terminated early due to a potential safety signal of congestive heart failure.”
assertions.note: FDA's Category 2 table documents ibutamoren mesylate under 503A Category 2 due to a heart failure safety signal.

assertions.text: No sermorelin product is currently marketed in the US, and its historical FDA approvals were for pediatric GH deficiency and diagnostic testing.
assertions.note: The cited Federal Register source is a bot-blocked landing page and does not contain the substantive determination text.

units.text:
Why does a 'low' IGF-1 in a healthy 60-year-old not, on its own, justify growth-hormone therapy?
Explanation: Treat confirmed deficiency, not ageing: age-adjusted ranges plus the healthy-ageing trials.
Correct answer: IGF-1 falls normally with age, and trials in healthy older adults show small body-composition gains with more oedema, joint pain and glucose problems.
Explanation: Correct. The somatopause is physiology, and the trials point against treatment.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because growth hormone has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: GH acts on dermal fibroblasts, and GH excess visibly changes skin. The problem is the balance of benefit and harm in healthy adults.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because IGF-1 cannot be measured reliably.
Explanation: IGF-1 is a standard test. The point is to read it against an age-matched range and to treat…

units.text:
In GRADE, what does a certainty rating attach to?
Explanation: Name the outcome before you name the grade; risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias can each lower it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A single well-run trial.
Explanation: GRADE rates a body of evidence, never one study on its own.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The molecule, across all its uses.
Explanation: The same molecule can be high certainty for one outcome and very low for another.
Correct answer: A body of evidence for a specific outcome.
Explanation: Correct. Certainty belongs to an outcome, across the studies that address it.

assertions.text: In GRADE, certainty/quality ratings are applied to a body of evidence rather than individual studies.
assertions.quote: GRADE specifies four categories-high, moderate, low, and very low-that are applied to a body of evidence, not to individual studies.
assertions.note: Balshem et al. (2011) state that GRADE categories are applied to a body of evidence and not individual studies.

assertions.text: In GRADE, quality ratings can be compromised or lowered by risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, and publication bias.
assertions.quote: "Quality" as used in GRADE means more than risk of bias and so may also be compromised by imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness of study results, and publication bias.
assertions.note: Balshem et al. (2011) list imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, and publication bias alongside risk of bias as factors compromising quality.

units.text:
Under section 503A, in what order does the statute let a bulk substance qualify for compounding?
Explanation: The statute's routes are hierarchical, and as of September 2026 no peptide sits on the six-substance bulks list.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The bulks list first, then a monograph, then a component of an approved drug.
Explanation: Reversed. The bulks list is the last route, open only when the first two are not.
Correct answer: A USP or NF monograph first, then a component of an approved drug, then the 503A bulks list, with a valid certificate of analysis in every case.
Explanation: Correct. The routes are hierarchical, and the certificate and a registered manufacturer are conditions throughout.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Any substance whose certificate of analysis shows high purity.
Explanation: A certificate is a condition, never a route on …

assertions.text: Under FD&C Act section 503A, bulk drug substances qualify for compounding hierarchically: first by complying with an applicable USP or NF monograph; if no monograph exists, by being components of FDA-approved drugs; or if neither applies, by appearing on FDA's 503A bulks list, accompanied in every case by a valid certificate of analysis from a registered manufacturer.
assertions.quote:
State-licensed physicians and pharmacists that compound under section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) may only compound drug products using bulk drug substances that:

Comply with an applicable United States Pharmacopeia (USP) or National Formulary (NF) monograph if one exists, and the USP chapter on pharmacy compounding;

Are components of FDA-approved drug products if an applicable USP or NF monograph does not exist; or

Appear on FDA’s list of bulk drug substances that can be used in compounding (the 503A bulks list) if such a monograph does not exist and the substance is not a component of an FDA-approved drug product.

In addition, bulk drug substances must be accompanied by a valid certificate of analysis and must have been manufactured by an establishment registered with FDA under section 510 of the FD&C Act.
assertions.note: Section 503A and FDA guidance explicitly state the hierarchical order and the requirement for a valid certificate of analysis.

assertions.text: As of September 2026, no peptide sits on the six-substance 503A bulks list.

units.text: The Hormone Cell Atlas (Fei, Huang-Doran et al., Science 2026) read RNA for 379 hormone and receptor genes in about 14 million cells and nuclei from 47 human tissues, skin included, and predicted which cell types could make or respond to hormones. Its own authors call these predictions putative and hypothesis-generating: RNA shows capacity, not secretion or effect. Treat any 'skin has receptors for it' product claim as a hypothesis until protein, function and a human trial back it. A few skin outputs are established in people, such as vitamin D3 formed under UVB and released into the blood.

units.text: Senescent cells accumulate in human epidermis and dermis with age, and in one cohort their number tracked with wrinkles and perceived age: an association. Their secretions (the SASP: IL-6, IL-8, matrix-degrading enzymes) were defined in cultured cells. Evidence that clearing senescent cells improves ageing comes from mice; human data are small open-label or exploratory pilots measuring tissue markers, and no randomized trial with clinical skin-ageing outcomes was found (September 2026). The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide advises confining senolytics to clinical trials. This course gives no doses or product advice; daily sunscreen and topical retinoids are the levers with human trials, and a prescriber decides on any treatment.

assertions.note: Waaijer et al. (2016) found that p16INK4a-positive epidermal and dermal cells were significantly associated with facial wrinkles and perceived age in 178 participants.

units.text: Most 'cortisol face' is puffiness from sleep, alcohol, salt and weight, as the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide describes it. Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is rare (two to three new cases per million people a year), and its commonest form comes from a glucocorticoid the patient is using, so ask about tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-lighteners. The features that best discriminate Cushing's are easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal muscle weakness and reddish-purple striae wider than 1 cm; a round face alone is a weak signal. If several are present and progressing, the next step is formal testing arranged by a prescriber and an endocrinologist, not a supplement or a consumer cortisol panel. Local skin cortisol (11β-HSD1) is a research mechanism with no approved treatment.

units.text: Estrogen acts on receptors in skin. In small trials, hormone therapy thickened skin and raised collagen (graded C here). The largest trial on facial skin (485 women, 48 weeks) and a four-year trial in recently menopausal women found no difference in wrinkles. In the US, as of February 2026, approved uses of menopausal hormone therapy are hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms and, for some products, preventing bone loss; skin is not an indication and is never the reason to start. Compounded 'bioidentical' hormones lack efficacy and safety data, and an over-the-counter 'hormone cream' is an unapproved drug under US rules. For skin, daily sunscreen and a prescription retinoid have better evidence. This course gives no doses; hormone therapy decisions belong with a prescriber.

units.text: Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is an MC1R agonist approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria (EU 2014, US 2019), on the strength of two sponsor-funded phase 3 trials; even there, the US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year. Melanotan II is a different, non-selective molecule approved for no indication. Its only controlled human data are two tiny 1990s studies, and case reports describe darkening and new moles, nail pigmentation, melanomas in people with other risk factors (causation unproven), priapism and rhabdomyolysis. FDA (April 2026), MHRA (April 2024) and TGA (August 2026) have all put warnings on record. If someone has used it: stop, record the product and seller, examine the skin and nails, and refer changing moles; a personal or family history of melanoma makes it an absolute no in the endocrinology guide. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice.

units.text: Signs of growth-hormone excess include puffy, thickened skin of the face, hands and feet, oily skin, more sweating, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, tight rings or shoes, night-time tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. On GH-axis drugs, fluid retention with swelling and joint pain is common and usually settles when treatment stops. The Endocrine Society recommends IGF-1 testing when typical acral and facial features are present, so route these patients to a prescriber or to endocrinology. On cancer, keep four answers apart: the IGF-1 receptor drives cell growth (mechanism); higher natural IGF-1 goes with modestly higher risk of some cancers (observation); GH replacement in true deficiency has not shown a clear risk in large cohorts; and for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for skin, long-term cancer data do not exist (open question).

assertions.text: Signs of growth-hormone excess include puffy, thickened skin of the face, hands and feet, oily skin, more sweating, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, tight rings or shoes, night-time tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms.
assertions.quote: Skin puffiness due to dermal glycosaminoglycan accumulation and edema are most prominent in the face, hands and feet. Oily skin with large pores, hypertrichosis, and excessive sweating are common features. Pigmented skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, and psoriasis are also encountered.
assertions.note: The cited text confirms cutaneous changes including puffiness of face/hands/feet, oily skin, sweating, skin tags, and acanthosis nigricans, but does not mention tight rings/shoes or night-time tingling.

assertions.text: On GH-axis drugs, fluid retention with swelling and joint pain is common and usually settles when treatment stops.
assertions.quote: Fluid retention may occur during EGRIFTA WR therapy and is thought to be related to the induction of GH secretion. This manifests as increased tissue turgor and musculoskeletal discomfort resulting in adverse reactions (e.g. edema, arthralgia, and carpal tunnel syndrome) which are either transient or resolve with discontinuation of treatment.
assertions.note: The label notes fluid retention causing edema and arthralgia that resolves upon treatment discontinuation.

assertions.text: The Endocrine Society recommends IGF-1 testing when typical acral and facial features are present.
assertions.note: The provided abstract of the Endocrine Society guideline does not state the specific recommendation for IGF-1 testing when acral and facial features are present.

recheck.note: The provided abstract for the Endocrine Society guideline (katznelson-2014-acromegaly-guideline) mentions addressing biochemical assessment generally, but does not include the specific recommendation for IGF-1 testing based on typical acral and facial features.

assertions.text: The IGF-1 pathway/IGF-1 drives cell growth and survival.
assertions.quote: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-I and its main binding protein, IGFBP-3, modulate cell growth and survival, and are thought to be important in tumour development.
assertions.note: The meta-analysis notes that IGF-I modulates cell growth and survival.

assertions.text: Higher natural IGF-1 is associated with a modestly higher risk of some cancers.
assertions.quote: Circulating concentrations of IGF-I and IGFBP-3 are associated with an increased risk of common cancers, but associations are modest and vary between sites.
assertions.note: The meta-analysis confirms a modest association between higher circulating IGF-I concentrations and increased risk of common cancers.

assertions.text: GH replacement in growth deficiency has not shown a clear cancer risk in large cohorts.
assertions.quote: There was no clear raised risk in patients with growth failure without other major disease.
assertions.note: The large SAGhE cohort study found no clear raised cancer risk in patients treated for growth failure without other major disease.

assertions.text: For secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for skin, long-term cancer data do not exist.
assertions.note: The provided sources do not mention secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 use for skin or the lack of long-term cancer data for these specific uses.

recheck.note: None of the provided sources discuss the absence of long-term cancer data specifically for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for skin indications.

units.text: GRADE rates certainty for a specific outcome across a body of evidence: high, moderate, low or very low (the Hormonaly guides print A to D). Randomized trials start high; certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias. Industry-sponsored studies more often report favourable results (Cochrane, 2017), so ask who ran and paid for the trials. A grade is separate from legal status: check both, and never let a mechanism raise a grade. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice.

assertions.text: GRADE rates certainty for a specific outcome across a body of evidence: high, moderate, low or very low.
assertions.quote: GRADE specifies four categories-high, moderate, low, and very low-that are applied to a body of evidence, not to individual studies.
assertions.note: Balshem 2011 notes GRADE specifies four categories (high, moderate, low, very low) applied to a body of evidence.

assertions.text: In GRADE, randomized trials start high; certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias.
assertions.quote: Randomized trials begin as high-quality evidence, observational studies as low quality. "Quality" as used in GRADE means more than risk of bias and so may also be compromised by imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness of study results, and publication bias.
assertions.note: Balshem 2011 notes randomized trials begin as high-quality evidence and may be compromised by risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, and publication bias.

assertions.text: Industry-sponsored studies more often report favourable results (Cochrane, 2017).
assertions.quote: Industry sponsored studies more often had favorable efficacy results, RR: 1.27 (95% CI: 1.17 to 1.37) (25 papers) (moderate quality evidence), similar harms results RR: 1.37 (95% CI: 0.64 to 2.93) (four papers) (very low quality evidence) and more often favorable conclusions RR: 1.34 (95% CI: 1.19 to 1.51) (29 papers) (low quality evidence) compared with non-industry sponsored studies.
assertions.note: The 2017 Cochrane review found industry-sponsored studies more often had favorable efficacy results compared to non-industry studies.

units.text: In the US, a 503A pharmacy may compound only from a substance that meets a USP or NF monograph, or else is a component of an approved drug, or else is on the 503A bulks list (six substances, none a peptide, as of September 2026), and it needs a valid certificate of analysis. A certificate is the supplier's report on one lot: mass spectrometry for identity, HPLC for purity, plus endotoxin and microbial results. It cannot prove your vial is that lot, how it was stored, or that it is sterile or lawful. 'Research use only' products are labelled not for use in humans, and 'off-label' applies only to approved drugs. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice; for an individual patient, that is the prescriber's decision.

assertions.text: In the US, a 503A pharmacy may compound bulk drug substances only if they comply with USP/NF monographs, are components of approved drugs, or appear on the 503A bulks list, and are accompanied by a valid certificate of analysis.
assertions.quote: (I) comply with the standards of an applicable United States Pharmacopoeia or National Formulary monograph, if a monograph exists, and the United States Pharmacopoeia chapter on pharmacy compounding ; (II) if such a monograph does not exist, are drug substances that are components of drugs approved by the Secretary ; or
assertions.note: 21 U.S.C. § 353a sets these exact conditions for bulk drug substances used in pharmacy compounding.
